rules.statement: Convert RFC 7519 NumericDate values (JWT exp/nbf/iat, auth_time, DPoP iat, Unix-seconds parameters) through the non-throwing `NCode.Json` `DateCoercion.TryFromNumericDate`/`TryParseNumericDate` helpers, never with `DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds`/`FromUnixTimeMilliseconds`.
rules.why: The DateTimeOffset conversions throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException outside the representable range, so attacker-supplied values like `iat: 99999999999999` turn a protocol rejection into an unhandled server error.
rules.check: Look for new calls to DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds/FromUnixTimeMilliseconds, or ad hoc try/catch of ArgumentOutOfRangeException around Unix-time conversion.

rules.statement: Read NumericDate time claims as JSON numbers that may be fractional (e.g. via `JsonElement.TryGetNumericDate`/`TryGetPropertyNumericDate`), not as `long`/integer-only values.
rules.why: RFC 7519 allows non-integer NumericDate values and real clients send fractional `iat`, so integer-only reads reject valid input.
rules.check: Look for time claims read with TryGetInt64/GetInt64 or parsed as long instead of through the NumericDate accessors.

rules.statement: Do not read NumericDate time claims through lenient date accessors that accept date strings (such as `TryGetPropertyValue<DateTimeOffset>`); accept only a JSON number.
rules.why: A date string is not a NumericDate, and lenient parsing compares an offset-bearing string's local ticks against a UTC clock.
rules.check: Look for exp/nbf/iat/auth_time read with generic TryGetValue<DateTimeOffset> or DateTimeOffset string parsing instead of the strict NumericDate accessor.

rules.statement: Treat a time claim that is present but not a valid NumericDate as a validation failure, never as if the claim were absent.
rules.why: Ignoring an unreadable nbf lets a token be used early, and ignoring an unreadable exp means it never expires when expiry is optional, so the validator fails open.
rules.check: Look for validation code where a failed TryGet on nbf/exp/iat falls through to the 'claim not present' path instead of rejecting with the endpoint's error.

rules.statement: When adding a margin or skew to an externally supplied instant, use saturating arithmetic that clamps at `DateTimeOffset.MaxValue`/`MinValue` instead of plain addition that can overflow.
rules.why: A validated instant near the top of the range overflows when a retention margin is added, which throws a server error.
rules.check: Look for DateTimeOffset.Add/+ TimeSpan on token- or request-derived times with no clamping against MaxValue.
